cards.text: Saul has just been confirmed as Israel's king at Gilgal, and Saul and all the Israelites are rejoicing (1 Samuel 11:15). Then Samuel, the prophet who's been leading Israel, speaks to all Israel. He tells them he listened to everything they said, and he set a king over them.

cards.question: Samuel points to the new king walking before them. Then he talks about himself. How does Samuel describe himself?

cards.text: Then Samuel puts his whole record on trial before the LORD and the LORD's anointed king. Friend, I sweat when ONE person stares at my cookie box too long, and Samuel just invited a whole NATION to check his record.

cards.question: Samuel asks the people if he ever took anyone's ox or donkey, cheated anyone or took a bribe. If he did, what does he promise to do?
When Samuel asks, the people say he cheated or oppressed some of them.

cards.text: Samuel says the LORD and His anointed are witnesses that nobody found anything in his hand, and the people agree. Nobody has EVER looked at my apron and said, "Not a spot on it."

Samuel reminds them the LORD is the One who appointed their leaders and brought their fathers up out of Egypt. Now he's going to confront them before the LORD with all the righteous acts the LORD has done for them and their fathers.

cards.question: Samuel starts back when Jacob, the father of Israel's tribes, went to Egypt and the fathers cried out to the LORD. The LORD sent them Moses, Israel's great leader, and ___.

cards.text: Moses and Aaron brought the fathers out of Egypt and settled them right here in this place. Now they've got a home, friend.

cards.question: Once the fathers are settled in the land, they forget the LORD their God.

cards.text: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines and the king of Moab, who fought against them. That's not one overdue bill in the mailbox, friend, that's THREE.

cards.question: Under pressure from Sisera, the Philistines and the king of Moab, the fathers cry out to the LORD. What do they confess?

answers.text: They had mocked the LORD's prophets
They had robbed the LORD's altar

cards.text: They admit they served the Baals and Ashtoreths, false gods, and ask the LORD to deliver them so they can serve Him. So the LORD sends deliverers, and Samuel names them: Jerubbaal, also called Gideon (Judges 7:1), then Barak and Jephthah, all leaders who fought Israel's enemies, and one more.

cards.question: The last deliverer Samuel names is himself.
Samuel tells Israel the LORD delivered them from their enemies on every side, and they dwelt ___.

cards.text: Then Samuel brings it right up to now. When Nahash, king of the Ammonites, moved against them, they told Samuel no, they had to have a king.

cards.question: Samuel says they demanded a king even though they already had one. Who does Samuel say was already their king?

cards.text: Here's the king they chose, the one they requested, and the LORD has placed him over them. You ever hit "order now" at midnight, and then the box actually SHOWS UP on the porch?

cards.question: Samuel lays out an if. If the people fear the LORD, serve Him and obey His voice, and if both they and their king follow the LORD, Samuel says all will be well.
But if the people disobey and rebel, Samuel says the hand of the LORD will be ___ them, just like with their fathers.

cards.text: Then Samuel tells them to watch a great thing the LORD will do before their eyes. And he asks them, "Is it not the wheat harvest today?"

cards.question: It's the wheat harvest, and Samuel says he'll call on the LORD to send something. What?
Samuel says the thunder and rain will make the people know and see something. What?

answers.text: The evil of asking for a king
The strength of their new king
The LORD's care for their fields

cards.text: Samuel calls to the LORD, and that same day the LORD sends thunder and rain. You finally get a sunny day off, you step outside, and the sky goes BOOM.

cards.question: When the thunder and rain come, all the people greatly ___ the LORD and Samuel.

cards.text: They beg Samuel to pray to the LORD his God for them so they won't die, and they admit they've added the evil of asking for a king to all their sins. One beep from my smoke alarm and I'm confessing EVERY burnt batch I ever made.

cards.question: Samuel answers the scared crowd. What does he tell them first?
Samuel tells the people that after all this evil, they should stop following the LORD.

cards.text: Instead, he says, serve the LORD with all your heart, and don't turn aside after worthless things that can't profit you or deliver you, because they're empty. Pretty box. Nice ribbon. NOTHING inside.

cards.question: Samuel promises the LORD will not abandon His people, for the sake of His great name. What other reason does he give?

answers.text: He was pleased to make them His own
They had kept every one of His laws
Their offerings had always pleased Him

cards.question: Then Samuel talks about himself. He says it would be a sin against the LORD to stop ___ for the people.

cards.text: Samuel will keep teaching them the good and right way, too. Then comes his "Above all": fear the LORD, serve Him faithfully with all your heart, and consider the great things He has done for them.

cards.question: Samuel ends with a warning: if the people persist in doing evil, only their king will be swept away.
